posts.title: "Pride" is losing traction — even the BBC has noticed!
posts.description: The BBC has finally noticed that Pride is losing friends. Across Britain, Pride events have been cancelled or postponed, corporate sponsorship is becoming harder to secure, councils are withdrawing support and organisers themselves are warning that the old funding model is beginning to fail. The BBC has an explanation: rising costs, commercialisation, corporate “rainbow-washing”, political opposition, the trans debate and councils deciding that taxpayers’ money might be better spent elsewhere. All of those things matter. But there is another part of this story which its “In Depth” investigation somehow manages not to mention at all. In recent years, a disturbing succession of men involved with Pride organisations have been convicted of, or subject to professional findings concerning, serious sexual offences against children. One prominent Pride organiser was sentenced to 24 years in prison for the rape of a 12-year-old boy. That does not mean homosexuality and paedophilia are the same

posts.title: A Catholic Biblical Association without the Catholic?
posts.description: The Catholic Biblical Association has elected as its president a distinguished scholar who openly says: “I do not believe in Jesus as Lord.” There is nothing scandalous about Amy-Jill Levine saying that, she is admirably honest. She is a practising Jew. The extraordinary question is why an association constitutionally committed to Catholic biblical scholarship thinks the confession that Jesus Christ is Lord is apparently unnecessary for its highest office. At some point, we have to ask: what is the word “Catholic” actually doing? See my full report on this at Regina Unscripted

posts.title: How do we attract young men to the priesthood?
posts.description: Why would a young man be attracted to the priesthood today? It's actually incredibly simple - so why are we finding it so difficult to discern the direction the Holy Spirit is guiding us in? A young man entering seminary later this year tells us about his calling
